⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

- The format guard implements your suggested `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` check, applied to **both** `--base-ref` (the pre-existing flaw) and `--prev-release-tag`. Empty is allowed (first release has no base tag) — verified under `set -euo pipefail` that an empty value short-circuits cleanly and a valid tag passes.
- Verified the guard against a live injection attempt: a tag value of `agents-rel-20261009-075526"; touch /tmp/pwned; echo "pwned` reaching the script via the env var is rejected with `::error::…` + exit 1 and nothing executes. - Two new wiring tests pin the invariant: *"gh-812 rework: the untrusted tag name reaches the script only via env indirection"* (asserts no `${{` between `run: |` and the builder invocation, plus both env mappings) and *"gh-812 rework: the tag format is validated before the builder runs"* (asserts the regex and the `::error::` rejection).

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Pack release integrity (gh-812) and the rollback contract

Two releases with differing pack content must never share a version
string. Live 2026-10-09 (gh-812): the version ledger (`versions.json`)
push back to main is best-effort and never landed, so consecutive
releases recomputed the same bump and shipped two different
`sm_github-0.1.36.zip` files (075526 vs 091304); version-keyed consumer
caches ran mixed content and every fa machine-sm tick went red for
~25 min. The pipeline now guarantees:

- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`), falling back to
  `versions.json` only when the release/`gh` is unavailable. A failed
  ledger push can no longer make a release reuse a version that is
  already out there.
- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints; metadata like
  `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change). Byte-identical
  rebuilds keep their version — no churn.
- **Require sanity gate** — every built zip is unpacked and every literal
  relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's

**Thread 3** — the workflow: env-indirection + tag-format validation:

{"newText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"","oldText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs

          args=(--out dist)

{"newText":"- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`). A failed
  shipped-state read FAILS the release — a gh outage is transient (the
  next push retries) while a silently degraded base re-opens the
  collision; `--allow-unverified-base` opts into the versions.json ledger
  fallback as a deliberate operator decision. A failed ledger push can no
  longer make a release reuse a version that is already out there.

  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints — path + sha256 + mode;
  metadata like `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change), and the
  first-built zip at the already-shipped version is deleted from `dist/`
  before the rebuild so the release ships exactly one zip per agent per
  version. Byte-identical rebuilds keep their version — no churn.","oldText":"- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

Details:

- The format guard implements your suggested `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` check, applied to **both** `--base-ref` (the pre-existing flaw) and `--prev-release-tag`. Empty is allowed (first release has no base tag) — verified under `set -euo pipefail` that an empty value short-circuits cleanly and a valid tag passes.
- Verified the guard against a live injection attempt: a tag value of `agents-rel-20261009-075526"; touch /tmp/pwned; echo "pwned` reaching the script via the env var is rejected with `::error::…` + exit 1 and nothing executes. Under the old YAML-interpolation form that same string would have been spliced into the script text itself.
- Two new wiring tests pin the invariant: *"gh-812 rework: the untrusted tag name reaches the script only via env indirection"* (asserts no `${{` between `run: |` and the builder invocation, plus both env mappings) and *"gh-812 rework: the tag format is validated before the builder runs"* (asserts the regex and the `::error::` rejection).

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Pack release integrity (gh-812) and the rollback contract

Two releases with differing pack content must never share a version
string. Live 2026-10-09 (gh-812): the version ledger (`versions.json`)
push back to main is best-effort and never landed, so consecutive
releases recomputed the same bump and shipped two different
`sm_github-0.1.36.zip` files (075526 vs 091304); version-keyed consumer
caches ran mixed content and every fa machine-sm tick went red for
~25 min. The pipeline now guarantees:

- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`), falling back to
  `versions.json` only when the release/`gh` is unavailable. A failed
  ledger push can no longer make a release reuse a version that is
  already out there.
- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints; metadata like
  `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change). Byte-identical
  rebuilds keep their version — no churn.
- **Require sanity gate** — every built zip is unpacked and every literal
  relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`

PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,

{"newText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed, strict by default.**

Both degradation paths now **fail the release** unless the operator explicitly opts in with the new `--allow-unverified-base` flag:

1. `shippedCatalog()` (`ci/release_packs.mjs`): when `--prev-release-tag` was provided but the shipped catalog cannot be read, it emits `::error::` and **throws** — the release exits non-zero before any ledger write or publish. Your reasoning is encoded in the error text: a gh outage is transient (the next push retries), a silently degraded release is the failure mode this pipeline exists to prevent. With `--allow-unverified-base` the fallback to the versions.json ledger still exists, but as a deliberate decision surfaced at `::error::`→`::warning::` level, never silently.
2. `shippedZipManifest()`: a missing/unreadable shipped zip used to return `null` → `fingerprintsDiffer(null, …) === false` → drifted payload shipped under the version that already shipped, per agent and quiet. It now also emits `::error::` and **throws**; `null` is only ever returned in the explicit flag mode or when there is genuinely no previous release to compare against (`!PREV_TAG` / dry run).

The workflow is unchanged on this point — it does **not** pass `--allow-unverified-base`, so CI keeps the strict default (asserted by a new wiring test: *"gh-812 rework: the workflow keeps the strict default"*).

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Pack release integrity (gh-812) and the rollback contract

Two releases with differing pack content must never share a version
string. Live 2026-10-09 (gh-812): the version ledger (`versions.json`)
push back to main is best-effort and never landed, so consecutive
releases recomputed the same bump and shipped two different
`sm_github-0.1.36.zip` files (075526 vs 091304); version-keyed consumer
caches ran mixed content and every fa machine-sm tick went red for
~25 min. The pipeline now guarantees:

- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`), falling back to
  `versions.json` only when the release/`gh` is unavailable. A failed
  ledger push can no longer make a release reuse a version that is
  already out there.
- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints; metadata like
  `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change). Byte-identical
  rebuilds keep their version — no churn.
- **Require sanity gate** — every built zip is unpacked and every literal
  relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.

Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
alone because it only ever lands on armed (`pr_approved`) PRs. Reviews of
PRs born without an issue: `review-external-once` (any non-machine author,
green checks, once — `ai_pr_reviewed` blocks re-review on later pushes),
`review-machine-unlinked` (the machine-author twin: a validated MACHINE PR
whose branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue — `develop-done` only
backfills open issues and `review-after-dev` rides the issue carrier, so
without this rule such PRs starve validated-but-never-reviewed; no checks
requirement because silent-updated heads read `none`, dedup rides the
leg's own check run flipping the rollup to `pending`; `prMachineAuthor`
fails closed when no machineAuthor is configured) and `review-on-label`
(`agent:review` on the PR, any author; the review runner consumes the
label). PR-anchored factory dispatches pass `pr`
instead of `issue`; the anchor rides the `pr-N` contextId into the agent
scripts (`preparePRForReview` / `postPRReviewComments`).

{"newText":"- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`). A failed
  shipped-state read FAILS the release — a gh outage is transient (the
  next push retries) while a silently degraded base re-opens the
  collision; `--allow-unverified-base` opts into the versions.json ledger
  fallback as a deliberate operator decision. A failed ledger push can no
  longer make a release reuse a version that is already out there.
- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints — path + sha256 + mode;
  metadata like `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change), and the
  first-built zip at the already-shipped version is deleted from `dist/`
  before the rebuild so the release ships exactly one zip per agent per
  version. Byte-identical rebuilds keep their version — no churn.","oldText":"- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

        id: build
        env:

          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}

          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash

          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed, strict by default.**

Both degradation paths now **fail the release** unless the operator explicitly opts in with the new `--allow-unverified-base` flag:

1. `shippedCatalog()` (`ci/release_packs.mjs`): when `--prev-release-tag` was provided but the shipped catalog cannot be read, it emits `::error::` and **throws** — the release exits non-zero before any ledger write or publish. Your reasoning is encoded in the error text: a gh outage is transient (the next push retries), a silently degraded release is the failure mode this pipeline exists to prevent. With `--allow-unverified-base` the fallback to the versions.json ledger still exists, but as a deliberate decision surfaced at `::error::`→`::warning::` level, never silently.
2. `shippedZipManifest()`: a missing/unreadable shipped zip used to return `null` → `fingerprintsDiffer(null, …) === false` → drifted payload shipped under the version that already shipped, per agent and quiet. It now also emits `::error::` and **throws**; `null` is only ever returned in the explicit flag mode or when there is genuinely no previous release to compare against (`!PREV_TAG` / dry run).

The workflow is unchanged on this point — it does **not** pass `--allow-unverified-base`, so CI keeps the strict default (asserted by a new wiring test: *"gh-812 rework: the workflow keeps the strict default"*).

New wiring tests in `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`:

- *"a failed shipped-catalog read FAILS the release (no silent ledger fallback)"* — asserts `throw new Error` + `::error::` inside `shippedCatalog()`;
- *"the ledger fallback is an explicit --allow-unverified-base decision"* — asserts `hasFlag('--allow-unverified-base')` and that the opt-in path stays visible at `::warning::` level;
- *"a failed shipped-zip read FAILS the release instead of skipping the drift check"* — asserts `throw new Error` + `::error::` inside `shippedZipManifest()`.

(The previous wiring test asserting "shipped-state reads degrade with a warning, never crash the build" was rewritten — it pinned exactly the best-effort behavior this thread flagged.)

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION — implemented.**

`shippedCatalog()` (`ci/release_packs.mjs`) now does **one batched download** right after the catalog read:

The gate extracts to its own temp dir and throws on unresolved requires, while `validatePack` re-reads per-entry bytes for hashing; sharing the tree would couple the two failure domains for a modest time win. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:

  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then

```

# gh-812 rework — all 6 open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 1)** — the payload-drift re-version path left the first-built `<agent>-<shippedVersion>.zip` (+ `.sha256`) in `dist/`, and `gh release create dist/*.zip` uploaded it: a collision-protected release still published two different packs under the same version. **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 2)** — the gh-failure fallbacks (`shippedCatalog()` → ledger, `shippedZipManifest()` → `null`/skip drift check) silently re-opened AC2 with only a `::warning::`. **Fixed: strict by default — both now fail the release; degradation requires an explicit `--allow-unverified-base` flag** (the stronger of the two suggested hardenings). The workflow passes no flag, so CI keeps the strict default.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 3)** — untrusted `agents-rel-*` tag names were template-expanded directly into the build step's shell (`--prev-release-tag`, plus the pre-existing `--base-ref`). **Fixed via `env:` indirection + `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` format validation for both.**
- 💡 **Suggestions (threads 4, 5, 6)** — all three implemented (comment fix, `mode` in the payload fingerprint, batched shipped-state download).
- Threads 7 (review summary) and 8 (rework-armed notice) are top-level PR comments with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; thread 7's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed above/below.
- The two `test_reviewVerdicts.js` failures (gh-807 round 3) remain pre-existing: re-verified to reproduce on a clean tree with this rework's diff stashed — untouched subsystem.
- Thread 6's *optional* follow-up (reuse the require-gate's extracted tree for `validatePack`) was deliberately not taken — noted in the thread reply.

## Approach

TDD for every finding — the tests were written/updated first and confirmed RED (9 failing), then the minimum code change turned them GREEN:

1. **Stale-artifact deletion (thread 1)** — in `buildPackRelease`, after `resolveShipVersion(next, true)` and **before** `buildPack(agent, next)`:
   ```js
   rmSync(zip, { force: true });
   rmSync(`${zip}.sha256`, { force: true });
   ```
   Ordering ahead of the rebuild makes "exactly one zip per agent in `dist/` at publish time" hold by construction.
2. **Fail-fast shipped-state reads (thread 2)** — `shippedCatalog()` and `shippedZipManifest()` emit `::error::` and throw on read failure when `--prev-release-tag` was provided; `--allow-unverified-base` gates the old warning-and-degrade behavior as a deliberate operator decision. The old "degrade with a warning, never crash" wiring test — which pinned the flagged behavior — was rewritten to pin the new contract.
3. **Tag-name hardening (thread 3)** — `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` env vars replace both `${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}` interpolations; a validation loop rejects any non-`agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` value (`::error::` + exit 1; empty allowed for the first release). Injection verified manually: a crafted tag value is rejected, nothing executes.
4. **Comment fix (thread 4)** — `parts.pop(); // drop the file name — resolve against its directory`.
5. **Mode in the fingerprint (thread 5)** — `payloadFingerprint` emits `path:sha256:mode` triplets (`mode || ''` keeps older modeless manifests working); metadata (`version`, `sourceCommit`) still never counts as a change.
6. **Batched shipped-state read (thread 6)** — one `gh release download --pattern '*.zip'` at catalog time; `shippedZipManifest()` reads the local copy (no per-agent `gh` round-trip). This also collapses thread 2's per-agent transient-failure surface to one loud failure point.

Docs (`docs/machine-factory-integration.md`) updated to match: the release-integrity contract now documents the fail-fast default + `--allow-unverified-base`, the mode component of the fingerprint, and the one-zip-per-agent-per-version `dist/` guarantee.

## Files Modified

- `ci/release_packs.mjs` — stale zip + `.sha256` deletion in the drift branch; strict-by-default shipped-state reads with `--allow-unverified-base`; batched previous-release zip download; local `shippedZipManifest`; header docs
- `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` — `mode` in `payloadFingerprint` (+ V4 doc)
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` — corrected `parts.pop()` comment
- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` — env-indirected `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` + tag-format validation (no `${{ }}` left in the build step's `run:` block)
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` — release-integrity contract updated
- `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js` — rewired gh-812 suite: 7 new tests + 1 rewritten
- `js/unit-tests/test_packVersionGuard.js` — new "payload fingerprint covers manifest mode" suite (4 tests)

## Test Coverage

- **RED → GREEN**: the 9 new/updated tests failed first (2 mode + 7 wiring), then passed after the fixes.
- New wiring tests (`test_releasePacks.js`): stale zip/sidecar deletion ordered before the rebuild and `zipPath: rezipped`; `shippedCatalog`/`shippedZipManifest` fail-fast (`throw` + `::error::`); `--allow-unverified-base` opt-in stays `::warning::`-level; workflow carries no flag; exactly 2 `gh release download` calls with none per-agent; no `${{ }}` template expansion in the build script; tag-format regex + `::error::` rejection present.
- New unit tests (`test_packVersionGuard.js`): mode-only diff changes the fingerprint and trips `fingerprintsDiffer`; identical payloads (incl. modes) fingerprint identically; modeless manifests still fingerprint.
- Full suite: **2160 passed, 2 failed** — both failures (`test_reviewVerdicts.js`, gh-807 round 3) reproduce on a clean tree with this diff stashed (re-verified via `git stash`); pre-existing, untouched subsystem.
- Manual checks: `node --check ci/release_packs.mjs` clean; workflow validation loop exercised under `set -euo pipefail` (empty tag skips, valid tag passes, crafted tag rejected with exit 1 and no execution).
- AC4 (fa ticks green on the fixed release) stays a post-merge live verification, as flagged in the review.

        id: build
        env:

          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog

          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2

Both degradation paths now **fail the release** unless the operator explicitly opts in with the new `--allow-unverified-base` flag:

1. `shippedCatalog()` (`ci/release_packs.mjs`): when `--prev-release-tag` was provided but the shipped catalog cannot be read, it emits `::error::` and **throws** — the release exits non-zero before any ledger write or publish. Your reasoning is encoded in the error text: a gh outage is transient (the next push retries), a silently degraded release is the failure mode this pipeline exists to prevent. With `--allow-unverified-base` the fallback to the versions.json ledger still exists, but as a deliberate decision surfaced at `::error::`→`::warning::` level, never silently.
2. `shippedZipManifest()`: a missing/unreadable shipped zip used to return `null` → `fingerprintsDiffer(null, …) === false` → drifted payload shipped under the version that already shipped, per agent and quiet. It now also emits `::error::` and **throws**; `null` is only ever returned in the explicit flag mode or when there is genuinely no previous release to compare against (`!PREV_TAG` / dry run).

The workflow is unchanged on this point — it does **not** pass `--allow-unverified-base`, so CI keeps the strict default (asserted by a new wiring test: *"gh-812 rework: the workflow keeps the strict default"*).

New wiring tests in `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`:

- *"a failed shipped-catalog read FAILS the release (no silent ledger fallback)"* — asserts `throw new Error` + `::error::` inside `shippedCatalog()`;
- *"the ledger fallback is an explicit --allow-unverified-base decision"* — asserts `hasFlag('--allow-unverified-base')` and that the opt-in path stays visible at `::warning::` level;
- *"a failed shipped-zip read FAILS the release instead of skipping the drift check"* — asserts `throw new Error` + `::error::` inside `shippedZipManifest()`.

(The previous wiring test asserting "shipped-state reads degrade with a warning, never crash the build" was rewritten — it pinned exactly the best-effort behavior this thread flagged.)

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

Details:

- The format guard implements your suggested `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` check, applied to **both** `--base-ref` (the pre-existing flaw) and `--prev-release-tag`. Empty is allowed (first release has no base tag) — verified under `set -euo pipefail` that an empty value short-circuits cleanly and a valid tag passes.
- Verified the guard against a live injection attempt: a tag value of `agents-rel-20261009-075526"; touch /tmp/pwned; echo "pwned` reaching the script via the env var is rejected with `::error::…` + exit 1 and nothing executes. Under the old YAML-interpolation form that same string would have been spliced into the script text itself.
- Two new wiring tests pin the invariant: *"gh-812 rework: the untrusted tag name reaches the script only via env indirection"* (asserts no `${{` between `run: |` and the builder invocation, plus both env mappings) and *"gh-812 rework: the tag format is validated before the builder runs"* (asserts the regex and the `::error::` rejection).

`shippedCatalog()` (`ci/release_packs.mjs`) now does **one batched download** right after the catalog read:

A new wiring test asserts the invariant structurally: exactly **two** `gh release download` occurrences remain in the builder (catalog.json + the batched zips), and none inside `shippedZipManifest()`.

The gate extracts to its own temp dir and throws on unresolved requires, while `validatePack` re-reads per-entry bytes for hashing; sharing the tree would couple the two failure domains for a modest time win. {"content":"# gh-812 rework — all 6 open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 1)** — the payload-drift re-version path left the first-built `<agent>-<shippedVersion>.zip` (+ `.sha256`) in `dist/`, and `gh release create dist/*.zip` uploaded it: a collision-protected release still published two different packs under the same version. **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 2)** — the gh-failure fallbacks (`shippedCatalog()` → ledger, `shippedZipManifest()` → `null`/skip drift check) silently re-opened AC2 with only a `::warning::`. **Fixed: strict by default — both now fail the release; degradation requires an explicit `--allow-unverified-base` flag** (the stronger of the two suggested hardenings). The workflow passes no flag, so CI keeps the strict default.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 3)** — untrusted `agents-rel-*` tag names were template-expanded directly into the build step's shell (`--prev-release-tag`, plus the pre-existing `--base-ref`). **Fixed via `env:` indirection + `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` format validation for both.**
- 💡 **Suggestions (threads 4, 5, 6)** — all three implemented (comment fix, `mode` in the payload fingerprint, batched shipped-state download).
- Threads 7 (review summary) and 8 (rework-armed notice) are top-level PR comments with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; thread 7's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed above/below.
- The two `test_reviewVerdicts.js` failures (gh-807 round 3) remain pre-existing: re-verified to reproduce on a clean tree with this rework's diff stashed — untouched subsystem.
- Thread 6's *optional* follow-up (reuse the require-gate's extracted tree for `validatePack`) was deliberately not taken — noted in the thread reply.

## Approach

TDD for every finding — the tests were written/updated first and confirmed RED (9 failing), then the minimum code change turned them GREEN:

1. **Stale-artifact deletion (thread 1)** — in `buildPackRelease`, after `resolveShipVersion(next, true)` and **before** `buildPack(agent, next)`:
   ```js
   rmSync(zip, { force: true });
   rmSync(`${zip}.sha256`, { force: true });
   ```
   Ordering ahead of the rebuild makes "exactly one zip per agent in `dist/` at publish time" hold by construction.
2. **Fail-fast shipped-state reads (thread 2)** — `shippedCatalog()` and `shippedZipManifest()` emit `::error::` and throw on read failure when `--prev-release-tag` was provided; `--allow-unverified-base` gates the old warning-and-degrade behavior as a deliberate operator decision. The old "degrade with a warning, never crash" wiring test — which pinned the flagged behavior — was rewritten to pin the new contract.
3. **Tag-name hardening (thread 3)** — `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` env vars replace both `${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}` interpolations; a validation loop rejects any non-`agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` value (`::error::` + exit 1; empty allowed for the first release). Injection verified manually: a crafted tag value is rejected, nothing executes.
4. **Comment fix (thread 4)** — `parts.pop(); // drop the file name — resolve against its directory`.
5. **Mode in the fingerprint (thread 5)** — `payloadFingerprint` emits `path:sha256:mode` triplets (`mode || ''` keeps older modeless manifests working); metadata (`version`, `sourceCommit`) still never counts as a change.
6. **Batched shipped-state read (thread 6)** — one `gh release download --pattern '*.zip'` at catalog time; `shippedZipManifest()` reads the local copy (no per-agent `gh` round-trip). This also collapses thread 2's per-agent transient-failure surface to one loud failure point.

Docs (`docs/machine-factory-integration.md`) updated to match: the release-integrity contract now documents the fail-fast default + `--allow-unverified-base`, the mode component of the fingerprint, and the one-zip-per-agent-per-version `dist/` guarantee.

## Files Modified

- `ci/release_packs.mjs` — stale zip + `.sha256` deletion in the drift branch; strict-by-default shipped-state reads with `--allow-unverified-base`; batched previous-release zip download; local `shippedZipManifest`; header docs
- `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` — `mode` in `payloadFingerprint` (+ V4 doc)
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` — corrected `parts.pop()` comment
- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` — env-indirected `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` + tag-format validation (no `${{ }}` left in the build step's `run:` block)
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` — release-integrity contract updated
- `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js` — rewired gh-812 suite: 7 new tests + 1 rewritten
- `js/unit-tests/test_packVersionGuard.js` — new "payload fingerprint covers manifest mode" suite (4 tests)

## Test Coverage

- **RED → GREEN**: the 9 new/updated tests failed first (2 mode + 7 wiring), then passed after the fixes.
- New wiring tests (`test_releasePacks.js`): stale zip/sidecar deletion ordered before the rebuild and `zipPath: rezipped`; `shippedCatalog`/`shippedZipManifest` fail-fast (`throw` + `::error::`); `--allow-unverified-base` opt-in stays `::warning::`-level; workflow carries no flag; exactly 2 `gh release download` calls with none per-agent; no `${{ }}` template expansion in the build script; tag-format regex + `::error::` rejection present.
- New unit tests (`test_packVersionGuard.js`): mode-only diff changes the fingerprint and trips `fingerprintsDiffer`; identical payloads (incl. modes) fingerprint identically; modeless manifests still fingerprint.
- Full suite: **2160 passed, 2 failed** — both failures (`test_reviewVerdicts.js`, gh-807 round 3) reproduce on a clean tree with this diff stashed (re-verified via `git stash`); pre-existing, untouched subsystem.
- Manual checks: `node --check ci/release_packs.mjs` clean; workflow validation loop exercised under `set -euo pipefail` (empty tag skips, valid tag passes, crafted tag rejected with exit 1 and no execution).
- AC4 (fa ticks green on the fixed release) stays a post-merge live verification, as flagged in the review.

**Thread 3** — the workflow: env-indirection + tag-format validation:

{"newText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |

{"content":"# gh-812 rework — all 6 open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 1)** — the payload-drift re-version path left the first-built `<agent>-<shippedVersion>.zip` (+ `.sha256`) in `dist/`, and `gh release create dist/*.zip` uploaded it: a collision-protected release still published two different packs under the same version. **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 2)** — the gh-failure fallbacks (`shippedCatalog()` → ledger, `shippedZipManifest()` → `null`/skip drift check) silently re-opened AC2 with only a `::warning::`. **Fixed: strict by default — both now fail the release; degradation requires an explicit `--allow-unverified-base` flag** (the stronger of the two suggested hardenings). The workflow passes no flag, so CI keeps the strict default.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 3)** — untrusted `agents-rel-*` tag names were template-expanded directly into the build step's shell (`--prev-release-tag`, plus the pre-existing `--base-ref`). **Fixed via `env:` indirection + `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` format validation for both.**
- 💡 **Suggestions (threads 4, 5, 6)** — all three implemented (comment fix, `mode` in the payload fingerprint, batched shipped-state download).
- Threads 7 (review summary) and 8 (rework-armed notice) are top-level PR comments with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; thread 7's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed above/below.
- The two `test_reviewVerdicts.js` failures (gh-807 round 3) remain pre-existing: re-verified to reproduce on a clean tree with this rework's diff stashed — untouched subsystem.
- Thread 6's *optional* follow-up (reuse the require-gate's extracted tree for `validatePack`) was deliberately not taken — noted in the thread reply.

## Approach

TDD for every finding — the tests were written/updated first and confirmed RED (9 failing), then the minimum code change turned them GREEN:

1. **Stale-artifact deletion (thread 1)** — in `buildPackRelease`, after `resolveShipVersion(next, true)` and **before** `buildPack(agent, next)`:
   ```js
   rmSync(zip, { force: true });
   rmSync(`${zip}.sha256`, { force: true });
   ```
   Ordering ahead of the rebuild makes "exactly one zip per agent in `dist/` at publish time" hold by construction.
2. **Fail-fast shipped-state reads (thread 2)** — `shippedCatalog()` and `shippedZipManifest()` emit `::error::` and throw on read failure when `--prev-release-tag` was provided; `--allow-unverified-base` gates the old warning-and-degrade behavior as a deliberate operator decision. The old "degrade with a warning, never crash" wiring test — which pinned the flagged behavior — was rewritten to pin the new contract.
3. **Tag-name hardening (thread 3)** — `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` env vars replace both `${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}` interpolations; a validation loop rejects any non-`agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` value (`::error::` + exit 1; empty allowed for the first release). Injection verified manually: a crafted tag value is rejected, nothing executes.
4. **Comment fix (thread 4)** — `parts.pop(); // drop the file name — resolve against its directory`.
5. **Mode in the fingerprint (thread 5)** — `payloadFingerprint` emits `path:sha256:mode` triplets (`mode || ''` keeps older modeless manifests working); metadata (`version`, `sourceCommit`) still never counts as a change.
6. **Batched shipped-state read (thread 6)** — one `gh release download --pattern '*.zip'` at catalog time; `shippedZipManifest()` reads the local copy (no per-agent `gh` round-trip). This also collapses thread 2's per-agent transient-failure surface to one loud failure point.

Docs (`docs/machine-factory-integration.md`) updated to match: the release-integrity contract now documents the fail-fast default + `--allow-unverified-base`, the mode component of the fingerprint, and the one-zip-per-agent-per-version `dist/` guarantee.

## Files Modified

- `ci/release_packs.mjs` — stale zip + `.sha256` deletion in the drift branch; strict-by-default shipped-state reads with `--allow-unverified-base`; batched previous-release zip download; local `shippedZipManifest`; header docs
- `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` — `mode` in `payloadFingerprint` (+ V4 doc)
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` — corrected `parts.pop()` comment
- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` — env-indirected `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` + tag-format validation (no `${{ }}` left in the build step's `run:` block)
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` — release-integrity contract updated
- `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js` — rewired gh-812 suite: 7 new tests + 1 rewritten
- `js/unit-tests/test_packVersionGuard.js` — new "payload fingerprint covers manifest mode" suite (4 tests)

## Test Coverage

- **RED → GREEN**: the 9 new/updated tests failed first (2 mode + 7 wiring), then passed after the fixes.
- New wiring tests (`test_releasePacks.js`): stale zip/sidecar deletion ordered before the rebuild and `zipPath: rezipped`; `shippedCatalog`/`shippedZipManifest` fail-fast (`throw` + `::error::`); `--allow-unverified-base` opt-in stays `::warning::`-level; workflow carries no flag; exactly 2 `gh release download` calls with none per-agent; no `${{ }}` template expansion in the build script; tag-format regex + `::error::` rejection present.
- New unit tests (`test_packVersionGuard.js`): mode-only diff changes the fingerprint and trips `fingerprintsDiffer`; identical payloads (incl. modes) fingerprint identically; modeless manifests still fingerprint.
- Full suite: **2160 passed, 2 failed** — both failures (`test_reviewVerdicts.js`, gh-807 round 3) reproduce on a clean tree with this diff stashed (re-verified via `git stash`); pre-existing, untouched subsystem.
- Manual checks: `node --check ci/release_packs.mjs` clean; workflow validation loop exercised under `set -euo pipefail` (empty tag skips, valid tag passes, crafted tag rejected with exit 1 and no execution).
- AC4 (fa ticks green on the fixed release) stays a post-merge live verification, as flagged in the review.

{"newText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"","oldText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"","path":".github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

Details:

- The format guard implements your suggested `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` check, applied to **both** `--base-ref` (the pre-existing flaw) and `--prev-release-tag`. Empty is allowed (first release has no base tag) — verified under `set -euo pipefail` that an empty value short-circuits cleanly and a valid tag passes.

- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 3)** — untrusted `agents-rel-*` tag names were template-expanded directly into the build step's shell (`--prev-release-tag`, plus the pre-existing `--base-ref`). **Fixed via `env:` indirection + `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` format validation for both.**
- 💡 **Suggestions (threads 4, 5, 6)** — all three implemented (comment fix, `mode` in the payload fingerprint, batched shipped-state download).

## Approach

TDD for every finding — the tests were written/updated first and confirmed RED (9 failing), then the minimum code change turned them GREEN:

1. **Stale-artifact deletion (thread 1)** — in `buildPackRelease`, after `resolveShipVersion(next, true)` and **before** `buildPack(agent, next)`:
   ```js

   rmSync(`${zip}.sha256`, { force: true });
   ```
   Ordering ahead of the rebuild makes "exactly one zip per agent in `dist/` at publish time" hold by construction.
2. **Fail-fast shipped-state reads (thread 2)** — `shippedCatalog()` and `shippedZipManifest()` emit `::error::` and throw on read failure when `--prev-release-tag` was provided; `--allow-unverified-base` gates the old warning-and-degrade behavior as a deliberate operator decision. 4. **Comment fix (thread 4)** — `parts.pop(); // drop the file name — resolve against its directory`.
5. **Mode in the fingerprint (thread 5)** — `payloadFingerprint` emits `path:sha256:mode` triplets (`mode || ''` keeps older modeless manifests working); metadata (`version`, `sourceCommit`) still never counts as a change.

{"newText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"","oldText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build

          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)

{"newText":"- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`). A failed
  shipped-state read FAILS the release — a gh outage is transient (the
  next push retries) while a silently degraded base re-opens the
  collision; `--allow-unverified-base` opts into the versions.json ledger
  fallback as a deliberate operator decision. A failed ledger push can no
  longer make a release reuse a version that is already out there.
- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints — path + sha256 + mode;
  metadata like `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change), and the
  first-built zip at the already-shipped version is deleted from `dist/`
  before the rebuild so the release ships exactly one zip per agent per
  version. Byte-identical rebuilds keep their version — no churn.","oldText":"- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`), falling back to
  `versions.json` only when the release/`gh` is unavailable. A failed
  ledger push can no longer make a release reuse a version that is
  already out there.
- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints; metadata like
  `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change). Byte-identical
  rebuilds keep their version — no churn.","path":"docs/machine-factory-integration.md"}

Both degradation paths now **fail the release** unless the operator explicitly opts in with the new `--allow-unverified-base` flag:

1. `shippedCatalog()` (`ci/release_packs.mjs`): when `--prev-release-tag` was provided but the shipped catalog cannot be read, it emits `::error::` and **throws** — the release exits non-zero before any ledger write or publish. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

Details:

- The format guard implements your suggested `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` check, applied to **both** `--base-ref` (the pre-existing flaw) and `--prev-release-tag`. Empty is allowed (first release has no base tag) — verified under `set -euo pipefail` that an empty value short-circuits cleanly and a valid tag passes.
- Verified the guard against a live injection attempt: a tag value of `agents-rel-20261009-075526"; touch /tmp/pwned; echo "pwned` reaching the script via the env var is rejected with `::error::…` + exit 1 and nothing executes. Under the old YAML-interpolation form that same string would have been spliced into the script text itself.
- Two new wiring tests pin the invariant: *"gh-812 rework: the untrusted tag name reaches the script only via env indirection"* (asserts no `${{` between `run: |` and the builder invocation, plus both env mappings) and *"gh-812 rework: the tag format is validated before the builder runs"* (asserts the regex and the `::error::` rejection).

{"content":"# gh-812 rework — all 6 open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **BLOCKING (thread 1)** — the payload-drift re-version path left the first-built `<agent>-<shippedVersion>.zip` (+ `.sha256`) in `dist/`, and `gh release create dist/*.zip` uploaded it: a collision-protected release still published two different packs under the same version. **Fixed.**
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 2)** — the gh-failure fallbacks (`shippedCatalog()` → ledger, `shippedZipManifest()` → `null`/skip drift check) silently re-opened AC2 with only a `::warning::`. **Fixed: strict by default — both now fail the release; degradation requires an explicit `--allow-unverified-base` flag** (the stronger of the two suggested hardenings). The workflow passes no flag, so CI keeps the strict default.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT (thread 3)** — untrusted `agents-rel-*` tag names were template-expanded directly into the build step's shell (`--prev-release-tag`, plus the pre-existing `--base-ref`). **Fixed via `env:` indirection + `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` format validation for both.**
- 💡 **Suggestions (threads 4, 5, 6)** — all three implemented (comment fix, `mode` in the payload fingerprint, batched shipped-state download).
- Threads 7 (review summary) and 8 (rework-armed notice) are top-level PR comments with no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; thread 7's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed above/below.
- The two `test_reviewVerdicts.js` failures (gh-807 round 3) remain pre-existing: re-verified to reproduce on a clean tree with this rework's diff stashed — untouched subsystem.
- Thread 6's *optional* follow-up (reuse the require-gate's extracted tree for `validatePack`) was deliberately not taken — noted in the thread reply.

## Approach

TDD for every finding — the tests were written/updated first and confirmed RED (9 failing), then the minimum code change turned them GREEN:

1. **Stale-artifact deletion (thread 1)** — in `buildPackRelease`, after `resolveShipVersion(next, true)` and **before** `buildPack(agent, next)`:
   ```js
   rmSync(zip, { force: true });
   rmSync(`${zip}.sha256`, { force: true });
   ```
   Ordering ahead of the rebuild makes "exactly one zip per agent in `dist/` at publish time" hold by construction.
2. **Fail-fast shipped-state reads (thread 2)** — `shippedCatalog()` and `shippedZipManifest()` emit `::error::` and throw on read failure when `--prev-release-tag` was provided; `--allow-unverified-base` gates the old warning-and-degrade behavior as a deliberate operator decision. The old "degrade with a warning, never crash" wiring test — which pinned the flagged behavior — was rewritten to pin the new contract.
3. **Tag-name hardening (thread 3)** — `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` env vars replace both `${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}` interpolations; a validation loop rejects any non-`agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` value (`::error::` + exit 1; empty allowed for the first release). Injection verified manually: a crafted tag value is rejected, nothing executes.
4. **Comment fix (thread 4)** — `parts.pop(); // drop the file name — resolve against its directory`.
5. **Mode in the fingerprint (thread 5)** — `payloadFingerprint` emits `path:sha256:mode` triplets (`mode || ''` keeps older modeless manifests working); metadata (`version`, `sourceCommit`) still never counts as a change.
6. **Batched shipped-state read (thread 6)** — one `gh release download --pattern '*.zip'` at catalog time; `shippedZipManifest()` reads the local copy (no per-agent `gh` round-trip). This also collapses thread 2's per-agent transient-failure surface to one loud failure point.

Docs (`docs/machine-factory-integration.md`) updated to match: the release-integrity contract now documents the fail-fast default + `--allow-unverified-base`, the mode component of the fingerprint, and the one-zip-per-agent-per-version `dist/` guarantee.

## Files Modified

- `ci/release_packs.mjs` — stale zip + `.sha256` deletion in the drift branch; strict-by-default shipped-state reads with `--allow-unverified-base`; batched previous-release zip download; local `shippedZipManifest`; header docs
- `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` — `mode` in `payloadFingerprint` (+ V4 doc)
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` — corrected `parts.pop()` comment
- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` — env-indirected `BASE_REF`/`PREV_RELEASE_TAG` + tag-format validation (no `${{ }}` left in the build step's `run:` block)
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` — release-integrity contract updated
- `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js` — rewired gh-812 suite: 7 new tests + 1 rewritten
- `js/unit-tests/test_packVersionGuard.js` — new "payload fingerprint covers manifest mode" suite (4 tests)

## Test Coverage

- **RED → GREEN**: the 9 new/updated tests failed first (2 mode + 7 wiring), then passed after the fixes.
- New wiring tests (`test_releasePacks.js`): stale zip/sidecar deletion ordered before the rebuild and `zipPath: rezipped`; `shippedCatalog`/`shippedZipManifest` fail-fast (`throw` + `::error::`); `--allow-unverified-base` opt-in stays `::warning::`-level; workflow carries no flag; exactly 2 `gh release download` calls with none per-agent; no `${{ }}` template expansion in the build script; tag-format regex + `::error::` rejection present.
- New unit tests (`test_packVersionGuard.js`): mode-only diff changes the fingerprint and trips `fingerprintsDiffer`; identical payloads (incl. modes) fingerprint identically; modeless manifests still fingerprint.
- Full suite: **2160 passed, 2 failed** — both failures (`test_reviewVerdicts.js`, gh-807 round 3) reproduce on a clean tree with this diff stashed (re-verified via `git stash`); pre-existing, untouched subsystem.

{"newText":"      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog

          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")

  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`). A failed

  collision; `--allow-unverified-base` opts into the versions.json ledger
  fallback as a deliberate operator decision. A failed ledger push can no
  longer make a release reuse a version that is already out there.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed, strict by default.**

Both degradation paths now **fail the release** unless the operator explicitly opts in with the new `--allow-unverified-base` flag:

1. `shippedCatalog()` (`ci/release_packs.mjs`): when `--prev-release-tag` was provided but the shipped catalog cannot be read, it emits `::error::` and **throws** — the release exits non-zero before any ledger write or publish. Your reasoning is encoded in the error text: a gh outage is transient (the next push retries), a silently degraded release is the failure mode this pipeline exists to prevent. With `--allow-unverified-base` the fallback to the versions.json ledger still exists, but as a deliberate decision surfaced at `::error::`→`::warning::` level, never silently.
2. `shippedZipManifest()`: a missing/unreadable shipped zip used to return `null` → `fingerprintsDiffer(null, …) === false` → drifted payload shipped under the version that already shipped, per agent and quiet. It now also emits `::error::` and **throws**; `null` is only ever returned in the explicit flag mode or when there is genuinely no previous release to compare against (`!PREV_TAG` / dry run).

The workflow is unchanged on this point — it does **not** pass `--allow-unverified-base`, so CI keeps the strict default (asserted by a new wiring test: *"gh-812 rework: the workflow keeps the strict default"*).

- *"a failed shipped-zip read FAILS the release instead of skipping the drift check"* — asserts `throw new Error` + `::error::` inside `shippedZipManifest()`.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed for both instances of the pattern.**

The build step in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` no longer contains any `${{ }}` template expansion inside its `run:` block. Both `steps.base.outputs.ref` consumers are routed through env indirection:

```yaml
env:
  BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
  PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
run: |
  set -euo pipefail
  for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
    if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
      echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
  [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
```

Details:

- The format guard implements your suggested `^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$` check, applied to **both** `--base-ref` (the pre-existing flaw) and `--prev-release-tag`. Empty is allowed (first release has no base tag) — verified under `set -euo pipefail` that an empty value short-circuits cleanly and a valid tag passes.
- Verified the guard against a live injection attempt: a tag value of `agents-rel-20261009-075526"; touch /tmp/pwned; echo "pwned` reaching the script via the env var is rejected with `::error::…` + exit 1 and nothing executes. Under the old YAML-interpolation form that same string would have been spliced into the script text itself.
- Two new wiring tests pin the invariant: *"gh-812 rework: the untrusted tag name reaches the script only via env indirection"* (asserts no `${{` between `run: |` and the builder invocation, plus both env mappings) and *"gh-812 rework: the tag format is validated before the builder runs"* (asserts the regex and the `::error::` rejection).
